title: Reinitialise the URL/set the URL and related note are not accurate
body:
(This has shades of https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/522.)

The spec currently says 

> When elements implementing the HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils mixin are created, and whenever those elements have their href content attribute set, changed, or removed, the user agent must set the url.
> 
> _NOTE: This is only observable for blob: URLs as parsing them involves the structured clone algorithm._

I badgered @annevk into adding this note because in jsdom's implementation, and IIRC in Chrome's based on comments from Adam, we try to avoid this kind of work, and do everything lazily. Indeed, the current spec is quite lazy, which is great, apart from this clause.

There is an exception however. Non-relative URLs hit line 1 of the "reinitialise url" algorithm:

> 1. If element's url is non-null and its non-relative flag is set, terminate these steps.

So for example, given a test like

``` js
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.setAttribute("href", "mycustomprotocol:abc");

  assert_equals(a.protocol, "mycustomprotocol:");

  a.href = "otherprot:test.js";
  assert_equals(a.protocol, "otherprot:");
```

this will fail in an implementation does not implement the "href content attribute set, changed, or removed" clause, even though no blob URLs are involved.

So, the note is inaccurate. **Solution number 1 to this bug is remove the note.**

However, I am not sure why the spec has the bailout in reinitialise url. It seems like a useless optimization that the spec should not be making. A real implementation that wants to optimize these things will do a lot of complicated stuff with dirty flags and base-url-change notifications and so on, which the spec doesn't capture. Why does it capture this one bail out case for non-relative URLs?

So, unless I am missing something, **solution number 2 to this bug is to remove reinitialise url and use set the url everywhere.** I think this would not be observably different and would allow the note about watching the attribute only mattering for blobs to remain true, which is great.
